$4B.origin: Early media reporting — Calcalist (Israeli tech press), July 19, 2023
$4B.what_it_represents: Initial estimate of total fraudulent LOCs on the Vesttoo platform, cited before full internal investigation was complete
$4B.accuracy: Rounded/estimated; widely repeated by industry press but not from a court filing

$3.36B.origin: Vesttoo's own interim investigation report filed with US Bankruptcy Court, District of Delaware (Case 23-11160), and independently confirmed by Artemis.bm and Browne Jacobson analysis of court documents
$3.36B.what_it_represents: The court-verified total of standby letters of credit (LOCs) assumed to have been fraudulently created — the precise investigated figure
$3.36B.accuracy: Court-filed; this is the primary-source verified number

$2.8B.origin: Two sources: (1) court-allowed claims figure (~$2.8B deemed allowable by bankruptcy court out of $4.8B filed), and (2) the China Construction Bank sub-total ($2.81B) of the $3.36B total
$2.8B.what_it_represents: Either the CCB-specific portion of the fraud, or the court-determined allowable creditor claims — NOT the total fraudulent collateral
$2.8B.accuracy: Technically accurate for what it represents, but incomplete as a total fraud figure

$4.8B.origin: US Bankruptcy Court, District of Delaware — aggregate creditor claims filed
$4.8B.what_it_represents: Total claims filed by all creditors (exceeds fraudulent LOC face value due to consequential damages, transaction failures, etc.)
$4.8B.accuracy: Court-filed figure; distinct from fraudulent collateral amount

primary_source.type: US Bankruptcy Court filing + independent investigation report
primary_source.court: US Bankruptcy Court, District of Delaware

recommendation.recommended_figure: approximately $3.4B in fraudulent letters of credit
recommendation.recommended_claim_text: Vesttoo's collapse in 2023 involved approximately $3.4 billion in fraudulent letters of credit (per the company's investigation report filed with the US Bankruptcy Court, District of Delaware, Case 23-11160); total creditor claims reached $4.8 billion
recommendation.rationale: The $3.36B figure is from Vesttoo's own court-filed investigation report and is the most precise, primary-source verified total of fraudulent LOCs. The $4B figure is a rounded early media estimate from before the full investigation concluded. The $2.8B figure conflates either (a) the CCB sub-portion alone or (b) court-allowed claims — neither represents total fraudulent collateral. Both artifact locations should use $3.4B (rounded from $3.36B) with a reference to the Delaware bankruptcy case.
recommendation.footnote_37_revision: Replace '$2.8B+' with '~$3.4B' and cite: Vesttoo investigation report filed with US Bankruptcy Court, District of Delaware, Case 23-11160 (2023); Artemis.bm coverage at https://www.artemis.bm/news/over-4-8bn-in-claims-levelled-against-vesttoo-entities-by-bankruptcy-creditors/
recommendation.PP6_5_cost3_revision: Replace '$4B in letters of credit' with '~$3.4B in fraudulent letters of credit' with the same citation — the $4B was an early unverified media estimate
recommendation.confidence: High — $3.36B is cross-confirmed by: (1) Vesttoo's own court-filed investigation report, (2) Artemis.bm analysis of court documents, (3) Browne Jacobson legal review, (4) Creditors' lawsuit complaint citing the same sub-breakdown (CCB $2.81B + StanChart $362.5M + Santander $186M = $3.36B)
